bandit.d: Treating the whole answer as a single action with a single reward, instead of a token-by-token MDP. It is the reading behind RLOO and behind GRPO with an outcome reward.

pass-at-1.d: Fraction of problems solved in a single attempt. Since one sample is noisy, papers generate several answers per problem (with temperature > 0) and report the average accuracy; it is the \(k=1\) case of pass@k.

avg-at-k.d: Average accuracy over \(k\) samples per problem (e.g. avg@32 in the DAPO ablation). It is pass@1 estimated with \(k\) samples to reduce noise.

cons-at-k.d: Consensus (self-consistency): sample \(k\) answers per problem and keep the most-voted final answer. It sits above pass@1 because errors scatter and the right answer tends to be the most frequent (R1-Zero, v1 of the paper: 71.0% pass@1 and 86.7% cons@64 on AIME 2024).

baseline-rl.d: Number \(b(x)\) subtracted from the reward in the policy gradient, \((R-b)\nabla\log\pi\). If it does not depend on the sampled answer, it does not change the mean of the gradient, only reduces its variance. It can be a critic, the greedy answer's score (ReMax) or the mean of other samples (RLOO, GRPO).

reinforce-pp.d: Critic-free method that normalizes the advantage with the mean and std of the global batch, not of the group; the KL enters either the per-token reward (k = 1) or the loss, as k2 (variant with a group baseline).

razao-de-importancia.d: \(r=\pi_\theta(a)/\pi_{\text{old}}(a)\): corrects the gradient when the data came from another policy. PPO and GRPO clip it per token; GSPO uses the sequence's geometric mean.

vantagem-de-grupo.d: Advantage computed only from the rewards of the \(G\) answers to the same prompt: \((r_i-\text{mean})/\text{std}\) in GRPO, \(r_i-\text{mean}\) in Dr. GRPO. It sums to zero within the group and is zero if the group is unanimous.

estimador-k3.d: \(k_3=x-\log x-1\), with \(x=\pi_{\text{ref}}/\pi_\theta\) at the sampled token. Unbiased and always \(\ge 0\), but it blows up when \(\pi_\theta\ll\pi_{\text{ref}}\) (16.0 with 0.01 versus 0.2). Compare with k1 \(=\log(\pi_\theta/\pi_{\text{ref}})\) and k2 \(=\tfrac12(\log x)^2\).

dr-grpo.d: “GRPO Done Right” (Liu et al., 2025): removes the division by the length \(|o_i|\) (it uses a constant MAX_TOKENS) and the division by the group std, eliminating the length and difficulty biases.

perda-por-token.d: Loss aggregation that divides by the total number of tokens in the batch, \(1/\sum_i|o_i|\), instead of averaging per answer. Every token weighs the same, and long wrong answers become the most punished (DAPO).

dapo.d: Decoupled Clip and Dynamic sAmpling Policy Optimization (ByteDance Seed and Tsinghua, 2025): GRPO without KL, with clip-higher (0.2/0.28), dynamic sampling, token-level loss and a soft punishment of long answers. It took Qwen2.5-32B base from 30 to 50 on AIME 2024.

clip-higher.d: Asymmetric clip \([1-\varepsilon_{\text{low}},1+\varepsilon_{\text{high}}]\) with \(\varepsilon_{\text{high}}>\varepsilon_{\text{low}}\) (0.28 and 0.2 in DAPO): lets rare tokens with positive advantage grow more, against entropy collapse.

amostragem-dinamica.d: Discarding groups in which every answer was right or every answer was wrong (all-zero advantage) and resampling until the batch is full. From DAPO; also called the zero-variance filter.

overlong-punishment.d: DAPO's extra reward: 0 up to \(L_{\max}-L_{\text{cache}}\), falls linearly to −1 at \(L_{\max}\) and stays at −1 after that (20,480 and 4,096 in the paper). In TRL: get_soft_overlong_punishment.

cispo.d: Clipped IS-weight Policy Optimization (MiniMax-M1, 2025): clips the importance weight with a stop-gradient, \(\operatorname{sg}(\hat r)\hat A\log\pi\), instead of cutting the update. No token, not even rare reflection tokens like “Wait”, loses its gradient.

gspo.d: Group Sequence Policy Optimization (Qwen, 2025): uses the sequence-level importance ratio, \(s_i=(\pi_\theta(y_i)/\pi_{\text{old}}(y_i))^{1/|y_i|}\), with a clip of \(3\times10^{-4}\)/\(4\times10^{-4}\). Stable on MoE without routing replay.

sapo.d: Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization (Qwen, 2025): replaces the clip with a sigmoid gate, weight \(4p(1-p)\) with \(p=\sigma(\tau(r-1))\), with \(\tau_{\text{neg}}>\tau_{\text{pos}}\). Used for the Qwen3-VL series.

f2p-p2p.d: Fail-to-pass: tests that failed before the patch and must pass after it. Pass-to-pass: tests that passed and must keep passing. Together they verify that the patch fixes the bug without breaking anything else.

recompensa-de-resultado.d: Score given only to the final answer (right or wrong, or the score of an outcome reward model). In GRPO it becomes the same advantage for every token.

recompensa-de-processo.d: Score given to each reasoning step, usually the probability that the step is correct; the solution's score is typically the product of the steps (Lightman et al.). Good for reranking, fragile as an RL target.

grm.d: An LLM that judges an answer by writing a critique and a score, often guided by rubrics. Used where there is no verifier (DeepSeek-GRM, V4 with the actor as judge, GLM-5).

rubrica.d: Per-instance checklist of criteria that a judge uses to score an answer; aggregated into a reward (Rubrics as Rewards) or multiplied by the test outcome (MiMo's GRS).

sobre-otimizacao.d: Optimizing too hard against an approximate reward model: its score keeps rising while the real quality (a “gold” RM) peaks and falls. Gao et al.: \(R_{\text{RL}}(d)=d(\alpha-\beta\log d)\), \(d=\sqrt{\mathrm{KL}}\).

opd.d: Distillation on the student's own samples, minimizing the reverse KL to one or more teachers. In the cheap form, the per-token advantage becomes \(\log\pi_{\text{teacher}}-\log\pi_{\text{student}}\) only at the sampled token (GLM-5, MiMo MOPD); DeepSeek-V4 uses \(\sum_i w_i\,\mathrm{KL}(\pi_\theta\,\|\,\pi_{E_i})\) over the whole vocabulary, because the per-token form had high variance.

colapso-de-entropia.d: The policy's entropy falling during RL until the group generates nearly identical answers and learning stops. It happens when already-likely actions get high advantage: \(\Delta H\approx-\operatorname{Cov}(\log\pi,\Delta z)\).

off-policy-sequence-masking.d: DeepSeek-V3.2 stabilizer: zeroes sequences with negative advantage whose per-token mean of \(\log(\pi_{\text{old}}/\pi_\theta)\) exceeds a threshold \(\delta\), with \(\pi_{\text{old}}\) coming from the inference engine.

keep-routing.d: Recording which experts the inference engine picked for each token during the rollout and enforcing the same routing during training (DeepSeek, since V3-0324).

r3-routing-replay.d: Records the inference engine's top-K routing masks and replays them when training an MoE; it reduces the training↔inference KL and prevents collapse. Used in MiMo-V2.

roteador-congelado.d: Not updating the MoE router's parameters during RL. In MiMo-V2.6, a trainable router unbalanced the load within 20 steps (CV 0.78 → 2.0); frozen, CV ≈ 0.7.
